note: Reviewed disposition for every surface whose backend authority disagreed with its filesystem position. A DISAGREES verdict is a QUESTION; this file is the answer, with the evidence that answers it.

decisions.reason: A platform operator provisions CUSTOMER organizations, so organization-scoped endpoints are the OBJECT of the administration, not evidence of tenant placement. The page is platform-gated and appears only in the platform admin navigation.
evidence: apps/web/components/admin/adminNavigation.ts — the entry carries scope PLATFORM_AUDIT
audit/ui-truth/data/access-matrix.json — every non-platform persona resolves PLATFORM_ADMIN_ONLY

decisions.reason: The commercial subject is the active workspace, and for an organization workspace that subject is the organization. Organization-scoped billing reads on a workspace surface are the documented model, not a placement error.
evidence: packages/shared-billing/src/plan-catalog.ts — PLAN_CAPABILITIES is keyed by the workspace's effective plan
services/api/src/services/billing/commercial-context.service.ts — resolveCommercialContext resolves the subject from the active workspace

decisions.reason: The page is a tenant surface and the endpoints behave as workspace-anchored at runtime: /v1/ops/incidents refuses a request without teamId and answers 404 for another tenant's workspace in both directions. The capability map labels them PLATFORM/PLATFORM_GLOBAL, which is what produced the disagreement. Placement stands; the label is the defect (UIT-001).
evidence: runtime: GET /v1/ops/incidents without teamId -> 400 INVALID_INPUT; with another tenant's teamId -> 404 not_found (org-owner -> personal workspace, and free-personal -> org workspace)
audit/ui-truth/data/runtime-authz.json — free/pro personas receive 404 for every /v1/ops read of the fixture organization workspace

decisions.reason: Same family as /operations: GET /v1/reliability/summary answers 200 for a member of the workspace, 404 for another tenant's workspace, and 403 for a read-only member. The PLATFORM_GLOBAL label does not describe the runtime scope.
evidence: runtime: /v1/reliability/summary own workspace 200, other tenant 404, read-only persona 403
audit/ui-truth/data/runtime-authz.json

decisions.reason: The organization list is assembled from the caller's own workspace memberships, so workspace-scoped reads are the correct source for it.
evidence: audit/ui-truth/data/placement.json — the surface consumes membership reads only

decisions.reason: A read-only organization governance view over external reviewer grants. The page states that issuance, revocation and rotation live on their canonical operator surface, so the single workspace-scoped read is a governance projection rather than a misplaced operator control.
evidence: apps/web/app/(app)/organizations/[id]/admin/governance/external-reviewers/page.tsx:393-406 — "Canonical surfaces" panel: "This governance view is read-only."

decisions.reason: An organization readiness view legitimately mixes organization posture with the workspace evidence that produces it; the page is reachable only inside an organization admin route whose gate requires the organization.
evidence: audit/ui-truth/data/access-matrix.json — requiredActiveSpace ORGANIZATION_ONLY

decisions.reason: Trust posture for an organization is computed from workspace-level evidence; the ten workspace reads are the inputs to the organization view, not a tenant surface hiding in an organization namespace.
evidence: audit/ui-truth/data/placement.json — reads are evidence/trust projections, no workspace mutation

decisions.reason: The page declares itself workspace-anchored and calls /v1/redaction/workspace/*; the capability map labels those endpoints ORGANIZATION_SCOPED. Placement stands; the tenancy label is inconsistent with the route's own contract (UIT-001).
evidence: apps/web/app/(app)/redaction/page.tsx:6-8,75-76 — "redaction projects are workspace-anchored; re-scope the whole page on a workspace switch"
docs/architecture/current-runtime-capability-map.json — GET /v1/redaction/workspace/summary tenantType ORGANIZATION

decisions.reason: Detail surface of the same workspace-anchored family; inherits the parent's contract and the same map labelling.
evidence: apps/web/app/(app)/redaction/page.tsx:13 — the detail route is the redaction workspace

decisions.reason: Policy editing for the same workspace-anchored family.
evidence: audit/ui-truth/data/placement.json — all reads are /v1/redaction/*

decisions.reason: Proven at runtime to be workspace-anchored: 200 for the org owner and workspace admin, 403 for another tenant's workspace, 403 for personal-space callers. The route file states the rule explicitly. The map's MULTI_TENANT_PLATFORM_ADMIN label is wrong (UIT-001).
evidence: services/api/src/routes/reviewer-workspace.routes.ts:26-27 — "Every route is workspace-anchored. Personal-space callers receive a bounded 403"
runtime: GET /v1/reviewer/disagreements own workspace 200, other tenant 403, free/pro personal 403

decisions.reason: Same route file and same runtime behaviour as /review/disagreements.
evidence: runtime: GET /v1/reviewer/qc/samples own workspace 200, other tenant 403

decisions.reason: GET /v1/coding/schemas answers 200 for tenant admins and 403 for another tenant's workspace, so the coding schema library is workspace-anchored despite the platform label.
evidence: runtime: GET /v1/coding/schemas own workspace 200, other tenant 403, read-only member 403

decisions.reason: Settings is deliberately one shell over account, workspace and organization panes, resolved by the canonical settings navigation model. Mixed tenancy is the design, and each pane names its own scope.
evidence: apps/web/lib/settings/settingsNavigation.ts — resolveSettingsNavigation composes account and workspace panes

decisions.reason: A delivery log for the active workspace's notifications sits under the ACCOUNT settings namespace. Nothing on the path says which workspace's deliveries are listed, and the two reads are workspace-scoped, so the page changes meaning on a workspace switch while its URL does not.
evidence: audit/ui-truth/data/placement.json — both endpoints are WORKSPACE tenancy
apps/web/lib/navigation/routeRegistry.ts — the route's domain is ACCOUNT
decisions.recommendation: Either move it under the workspace notification settings, or state the active workspace in the page header and re-scope on switch.

decisions.reason: Eleven workspace-scoped reads and writes for reviewer criteria live under ACCOUNT settings. The criteria belong to the workspace, not to the signed-in person, so an operator editing them from the account namespace cannot tell whose criteria they are changing.
evidence: audit/ui-truth/data/placement.json — 11 WORKSPACE-tenancy endpoints on an ACCOUNT-domain route
decisions.recommendation: Move under the workspace review settings, or make the active workspace explicit in the header and on every write confirmation.
